sentenceSets.sentence: The work achieved verisimilitude through accumulated specific detail rather than through any single dramatic effect.

answerChoices.reasoning: Realism means resemblance to reality or realistic depiction, which the work achieves, but verisimilitude specifically refers to the quality or state of appearing true.
Authenticity means genuineness or being true to origin, which the work has, but verisimilitude specifically refers to the appearance of truth.
Credibility means ability to be believed, which the work achieves, but verisimilitude specifically refers to the quality of appearing true.
Likelihood means the state of being probable or likely, which the work demonstrates, but does not specifically refer to the appearance of truth.
Accuracy means freedom from error or correctness, which the work might possess, but verisimilitude emphasizes appearance of truth more than accuracy.
Plausibility means the quality of being plausible or reasonable, which the work has, but does not specifically refer to appearance of truth.
Coherence means logical consistency or holding together, which the work demonstrates, but does not specifically refer to the appearance of truth.
Depth means profound or detailed quality, which the specific details provide, but does not specifically refer to the appearance of truth.
Falsehood means untruth or what is false, the opposite of verisimilitude or the appearance of truth.
Artificiality means being artificial or contrived, the opposite of verisimilitude achieved through accumulated specific detail.
Implausibility means the quality of not seeming reasonable, the opposite of verisimilitude or the appearance of truth.

Realism means resemblance to actual reality, which the documentary captures, but verisimilitude specifically refers to the quality or state of seeming true.

sentenceSets.sentence: The author's meticulous attention to period details created such verisimilitude that readers suspended disbelief despite knowing the story was entirely imagined.

answerChoices.reasoning: Realism means resemblance to actual reality, which the period details create, but verisimilitude specifically refers to the quality or state of appearing true.
Authenticity means genuineness or being true to the period, which the details achieve, but verisimilitude refers to the appearance of truth, not actual authenticity.
Credibility means ability to be believed, which the verisimilitude creates, but does not specifically refer to the quality of appearing true.
Plausibility means the quality of being plausible or reasonable, which the details produce, but does not specifically refer to the appearance of truth.
Accuracy means freedom from error regarding historical details, which the author achieves, but verisimilitude emphasizes appearance of truth.
Vividness means the quality of being vivid or lifelike, which the details create, but does not specifically refer to the appearance of truth.
Sophistication means refined quality or complexity, which the attention to detail demonstrates, but does not specifically refer to appearance of truth.
Immersion means complete engagement, which the verisimilitude creates, but is a result rather than verisimilitude itself.
Artifice means clever deception, whereas verisimilitude created through authentic detail is honest in its appearance of truth.
Implausibility means not seeming reasonable, the opposite of verisimilitude that suspends reader disbelief.
Anachronism means something from the wrong historical period, the opposite of the careful period details that create verisimilitude.
